title: Best Presentation Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a presentation designer: what the package should include, how to brief your deck, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: A presentation designer turns a crowded deck into slides that support what you say instead of competing with it. Projects go wrong when the content is not ready, the file is delivered in a tool you cannot edit, or fonts break on another computer. This guide helps you order a deck you can present and update with confidence.

faq.q: Which software should the deck be made in?
faq.a: The one you will present and edit in, usually PowerPoint, Keynote or Google Slides. Say so in the brief. A beautiful deck you cannot edit is a problem the day before your meeting.

faq.q: Will the designer write the content?
faq.a: Usually not. Most packages design your existing content and may tighten wording. Some offer storytelling or copywriting as an extra. Send final content to avoid paying for rework.

faq.q: Can I get a reusable template?
faq.a: Ask for one. A master template with layouts for titles, text, charts and images lets you build future decks yourself in the same style.
Fonts that are not installed on the presenting computer can break the layout. Ask for standard or embedded fonts, and for images that are licensed for your use.

A pitch deck for investors has a typical structure: problem, solution, market, business model, traction, team and funding ask. Look for designers with pitch decks in their portfolio if that is what you need.
